title: Wrenmere Castle
subtitle: A house of unfinished questions

rooms.name: The Gatehouse
rooms.line: Three brass wheels. One honest beginning.
rooms.ambience: Wet stone, a lantern in a leaded window, rain ticking on a slate roof.
rooms.method: Start with constraints, not guesses.

rooms.name: The Long Library
rooms.line: Every shelf has an order. Every account has a gap.
rooms.ambience: Low lamps, leather bindings and a narrow aisle that seems longer on your return.
rooms.method: Separate what is stated from what you assume.
rooms.secret: A maintenance slip inside a misfiled book

rooms.name: The Observatory
rooms.line: Two clocks can disagree without either witness lying.
rooms.ambience: Copper instruments, a revolving star chart and clouds moving over the dome.
rooms.method: Calibrate a measurement before trusting it.

rooms.name: The Map Room
rooms.line: The shortest line is not always the shortest journey.
rooms.ambience: A table of folded surveys, pins in the valley and an old footpath in green ink.
rooms.method: Model a route; distinguish possibility from proof.

rooms.name: The Glass Orangery
rooms.line: A small change travels further than its maker.
rooms.ambience: Mist on glass, citrus leaves and a light lattice above the potting bench.
rooms.method: Track the consequences of one move at a time.

rooms.name: The Museum of Questions
rooms.line: You are not the first person to sit with this question.
rooms.ambience: Specimen drawers, playable tables, soft footsteps and labels that admit uncertainty.
rooms.method: A surviving object and a complete explanation are different things.
rooms.secret: Three ways to think across time

rooms.name: The Clockmaker’s Workshop
rooms.line: Make a smaller problem inside the larger one.
rooms.ambience: Brass filings, three wooden spindles and the outline of a tool that is missing.
rooms.method: Plan backwards and solve the smaller case.

rooms.name: The Keeper’s Study
rooms.line: The house kept a record. It did not keep a fair one.
rooms.ambience: A sealed cabinet, a watermarked ticket and room enough to change your mind.
rooms.method: Could is not did. A possible route does not prove a journey.

rooms.name: The Unrecorded Stair
rooms.line: The missing room was not missing. It was left out.
rooms.ambience: A line beneath the skirting, a cold draft and a name scratched under the plaster.
rooms.method: Look for what the record fails to include.

rooms.name: The Winter Conservatory
rooms.line: Nothing here needs you to hurry.
rooms.ambience: A reading chair, an illustrated guest book and a view of the restored greenhouse.
rooms.method: Rest is part of attention, not a reward for exhaustion.
rooms.secret: Your discoveries, kept without a deadline

rooms.name: The Portrait Gallery
rooms.line: A likeness is not a life.
rooms.ambience: Layers of varnish, family portraits and an empty label.
rooms.method: Separate observation from interpretation.

rooms.name: The Long Dining Room
rooms.line: The seating plan remembers who was never invited.
rooms.ambience: Silver laid for thirteen and one chair near the service door.
rooms.method: Use position and exclusion together.
rooms.secret: The place setting outside the portrait

rooms.name: The Court of Testimony
rooms.line: An accusation needs more than a tidy story.
rooms.ambience: A small panelled hearing room and unevenly preserved witness accounts.
rooms.method: Test competing explanations, not just your favourite.

rooms.name: The Music Salon
rooms.line: The silence belongs to the phrase.
rooms.ambience: A covered piano, a mechanical music box and written notation for every sound.
rooms.method: Patterns include absence and timing.

rooms.name: The Old Kitchens
rooms.line: A recipe is a system of relationships.
rooms.ambience: Hanging copper, measuring jugs and a hearth long since swept clean.
rooms.method: Think in conserved quantities.

rooms.name: The Scullery
rooms.line: Some paths are reversible. Some are not.
rooms.ambience: A tiled basin and jugs with worn measurements.
rooms.method: Search states, not just moves.

rooms.name: The Dead Letter Office
rooms.line: Unsent is not the same as unwritten.
rooms.ambience: Sorted pigeonholes, undelivered letters and stamps from impossible dates.
rooms.method: Identify the encoding before decoding.

rooms.name: The Flooded Archive
rooms.line: What survived was not a neutral selection.
rooms.ambience: Tide marks on shelves and bundles lifted above the waterline.
rooms.method: Missing evidence can be systematically missing.
rooms.secret: A second version of the plans

rooms.name: The Cistern Vaults
rooms.line: Water follows a rule, not a reputation.
rooms.ambience: Stone tanks, valve markings and names cut into old pipes.
rooms.method: Connected systems share consequences.
rooms.secret: The gate that should have opened

rooms.name: The Yew Labyrinth
rooms.line: A better question can be a shorter path.
rooms.ambience: Birdsong, clipped hedges and a viewing platform above the dead ends.
rooms.method: Change representation when the current one traps you.

rooms.name: The Old Orchard
rooms.line: A useful boundary can make possibilities visible.
rooms.ambience: Young saplings beside the oldest surviving apple tree.
rooms.method: Match resources under local constraints.
rooms.secret: A planting plan in two eras

rooms.name: The Seven-Arch Bridge
rooms.line: Not every inviting challenge has a possible solution.
rooms.ambience: River reeds, engraved bridge stones and a broken approach.
rooms.method: An impossibility proof can be a complete answer.

rooms.name: The Boathouse
rooms.line: The journey changes when the boat is small.
rooms.ambience: Oars on hooks and a scale model of the river.
rooms.method: Model capacity and forbidden combinations.

rooms.name: The Chapel of Echoes
rooms.line: Not every question has one defensible answer.
rooms.ambience: Plain stained glass, a quiet alcove and unsigned marginal notes.
rooms.method: Keep deduction and interpretation separate.
rooms.secret: A reflection that changes no score

rooms.name: The Sundial Court
rooms.line: The same mark means something different at another hour.
rooms.ambience: Worn paving, measured shadows and an unobstructed horizon.
rooms.method: Specify the frame of reference.
rooms.secret: A shadow aligning with the old stair

rooms.name: The Paper Theatre
rooms.line: A toy can carry a serious idea.
rooms.ambience: Paper stages, folding scenery and an unfinished puppet.
rooms.method: Rotate the model, not the assumption.
rooms.secret: A child’s drawing of the real house

rooms.name: The Rookery
rooms.line: Messages travel through a community.
rooms.ambience: Feathers, letter tubes and a map of possible couriers.
rooms.method: Reason about connectivity and failure.
rooms.secret: A route with no single point of failure

rooms.name: The Knight’s Chamber
rooms.line: A move has a shape; a plan has a horizon.
rooms.ambience: A stone board set into the floor and an unfinished tour.
rooms.method: Look ahead without forgetting the state you are in.

rooms.name: The Number Cabinet
rooms.line: Constraint can produce surprising freedom.
rooms.ambience: Small drawers, counting pieces and a many-sided table.
rooms.method: Propagate what is certain before branching.

rooms.name: The Balancing Hall
rooms.line: A relationship can tell you more than a value.
rooms.ambience: Hanging balances and numbered door weights.
rooms.method: Use order before exact quantity.

rooms.name: The Model Village
rooms.line: What should remain when a mystery is solved?
rooms.ambience: An architectural model, empty lots and a view towards the real village.
rooms.method: Make repair a creative act, not a resource tax.
rooms.secret: Future building collections and bounded expansions

rooms.name: The Companion Hearth
rooms.line: A place feels different when someone notices your return.
rooms.ambience: Warm cushions, a window perch and small muddy footprints.
rooms.method: Practice patient observation.

evidence.title: The maintenance slip
evidence.text: Station clock: seventeen minutes fast. Observatory clock: checked against the noon signal. Adjustment deferred. Signed R. Finch.
evidence.question: What does a timestamp measure when the instrument is wrong?

evidence.title: The corrected ticket
evidence.text: The station ticket is stamped 21:17. Subtracting the documented 17-minute error gives 21:00. This dates Finch’s departure from the station, not his arrival at the tower.
evidence.question: What does this establish, and what does it leave open?

evidence.title: The green footpath
evidence.text: The surveyed footpath takes 7 minutes: station to bridge, 2; bridge to orchard, 3; orchard to tower, 2. These are the case’s stipulated travel times. The tower bell rang at 21:10 by its calibrated clock.
evidence.question: Is a feasible route evidence that someone actually took it?

evidence.title: The margin under the stairs
evidence.text: “Mara went down to the river. Not to save the collection. To warn the village.” The note has no signature. Its claim still needs corroboration.
evidence.question: A moving account is still an account, not a proof.

exhibits.title: A walk that cannot be taken
exhibits.summary: Euler’s bridge problem replaces scenery with connections. Try tracing a walk; then count what cannot change. An impossibility result is not a failed solve.
exhibits.history: Euler’s 1736 work showed that a route crossing each of the seven bridges exactly once is impossible. Our schematic preserves the connections, not the physical scale of the city.
exhibits.boundary: Documented mathematical history. The interactive diagram and wording are original adaptations.

exhibits.title: Nine numbers, one balance
exhibits.method: Use symmetry and a conserved sum
exhibits.summary: Swap the nine numbers until every row, column and both main diagonals total 15. The number in the centre helps the rest fall into place.
exhibits.history: The Lo Shu is associated with Chinese traditions about a patterned turtle. That is a legend, not a securely dated account of an invention. Gresham’s lecture discusses the diagram and later mathematical developments.
exhibits.boundary: The tradition is historical; the turtle story is labelled legend. Rotations and reflections are equally valid mathematical solutions.

exhibits.title: An object outlives its instructions
exhibits.summary: A board survives. A complete account of every ancient ruleset does not. Explore a modern probability model of four marked dice without pretending that model is an ancient rulebook.
exhibits.history: The British Museum dates board 120834 to 2600–2400 BCE. A tetrahedral die from Ur has marks on two corners. Here we explicitly assume four independent, fair binary outcomes to explore their sums.
exhibits.boundary: Documented objects; explicitly modern fair-dice model. This is not a playable reconstruction of the complete Royal Game of Ur.

introduction: You have been invited to catalogue Wrenmere Castle. The letter contains a key, a library card, and one request: before you put the house in order, find out who put its history out of order.
contentNote: The wider story concerns bereavement, a flood and a wrongful accusation. There are no jump scares or graphic scenes. You may explore the museum and puzzles without following the story.

chapter.title: The Seventeenth Minute
chapter.premise: In 1911, a flood took the life of the castle’s curator, Mara Vale. A clockmaker was blamed for returning too late to help. The ticket used against him is still in the house.
chapter.ending: You have not proved where Finch went. You have proved that the ticket does not establish that he was too late. Behind the study cabinet, a stair appears on the old survey but not the official plan. The house has more than one missing account.
